_comment: A LABELED SAMPLE of 75 REAL Senate roll calls, captured live from
senate.gov's public, keyless LIS XML feed during story 8.3 (2026-10-19)
from the confirmed-working endpoints:
index: .../LIS/roll_call_lists/vote_menu_{congress}_{session}.xml
item:  .../LIS/roll_call_votes/vote{congress}{session}/vote_{c}_{s}_{roll:05d}.xml
WHY A SAMPLE, AND HOW IT WAS DRAWN. Story 8.3's acceptance criterion is
'at least 95% accuracy on a labeled sample'. A sample drawn at random
from 1,606 live roll calls would be ~75% nominations and cloture motions
and would therefore measure almost nothing about the rare question
shapes, so this sample is STRATIFIED BY QUESTION instead: the live index
for congress 118 sessions 1-2 and congress 119 sessions 1-2 was fetched
in full (1,606 votes), its `question` field tabulated into the 34
distinct values that actually occur, and up to 3 real roll calls drawn
per distinct value (random.seed(42)). Every question shape the Senate
produced in two Congresses is therefore represented, including the
one-off impeachment-court and Point-of-Order questions that a random
sample would almost certainly have missed.
Three records were added deliberately on top of the stratified draw,
because they are the hard cases the stratification by `question` alone
cannot reach (the question text is identical to a common case; only the
item-level fields differ):
* motion-on-an-amendment (119-2:159) -- question 'On the Motion',
amendment_number populated, but the motion is a budget-point-of-order
WAIVER, not a vote on the amendment's text.
* cloture-on-an-amendment (119-2:240) and 119-2:226 -- question 'On the
Cloture Motion' with amendment_number populated; the case that proves
cloture must outrank the amendment signal.
HOW THE LABELS WERE ASSIGNED. By hand, from Senate practice and
datamodel.md's six-value vocabulary ('final_passage, amendment, cloture,
motion_to_recommit, procedural, other'), BEFORE the classifier under test
was written, and without consulting its output. The reasoning for each
family is recorded in app/ingest/senate_vote_typing.py's docstring. These
are the labels, not the classifier's predictions: the accuracy test
compares one against the other and fails if they disagree on more than 5%.
Each record carries only the item-level FIELDS the classifier reads, not
the whole XML document: the <members> list is ~100 elements per vote and
would make this fixture ~2MB for no test value. Story 8.1's own fixture
(senate_rollcalls_sample.json) holds full XML documents for the
transform/load path; this one holds classification inputs.
NO VOTER DATA, NO SYNTHETIC VOTES. Every row is the Senate's own official
public record of how it voted (CLAUDE.md's 'never put real voter data in
fixtures' rule is about voter profiles, which are political-opinion data;
a recorded Senate vote is a public act of government).
